title: Panang Chicken Curry with Makrut Lime Leaves and Peanuts
summary: A store-bought paste is boosted with toasted coriander, cumin and ground peanuts, fried in cracked coconut cream and simmered with sliced chicken thighs and red pepper until thick and glossy.
equipment: spice grinder or mortar and pestle

ingredients.item: store-bought panang or red curry paste
boneless, skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
makrut lime leaves, central rib removed (6 torn, 2 very thinly sliced)
palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.title: Boost the paste
steps.text: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in the dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant. Grind them finely, add the 30 g peanuts and grind to a coarse paste, then mix with the curry paste in the small bowl. Fresh-toasted spices and peanuts give a shop paste a much rounder flavour.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the fish sauce in the medium bowl. Thin slices take on the seasoning quickly and cook in minutes.

steps.title: Crack the cream
steps.text: Spoon 4 tbsp of the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into the large pan with the oil and cook over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until bubbling. Add the paste and fry for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until brick red and the oil separates, adding a splash of coconut milk if it sticks. Frying the paste in fat is what develops the curry's depth.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Add the torn lime leaves and sugar and stir for 1 minute. Set aside 2 tbsp coconut milk for serving, pour in the rest, bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and red pepper and simmer for 6-8 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through (74 °C) and the sauce is thick enough to coat it. Panang should cling rather than pool.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Drizzle with the reserved coconut milk and scatter with the sliced lime leaves, chopped peanuts and basil. Serve with jasmine rice.

tips: Do not shake the coconut milk can; you need the thick cream on top to fry the paste.
Curry pastes vary in saltiness and heat, so taste before adding more fish sauce.
Slice the lime leaves very finely, as large pieces are tough to eat.
Overcooking the sliced chicken is the commonest mistake; take it off as soon as it is cooked through.
storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 3 days. Reheat once until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
